analysis: Only docs/developer/test.md is in this batch: a date bump at line 3 and a rewrite of the release-lane test description in base lines ~1045-1052 (head 1048-1078). The supplied base text ends near line 939, so the changed hunk is visible only through the patch excerpt. No source, workflow, key-handling or runtime code is modified here, and the doc change alters no provider security control. The covered base text (provider/native test procedures, SSD cache test volume, add-on hold, App Attest dispatch, native serving qualification) is unchanged. It describes tests only and does not weaken TB-007/T-041, TB-011/T-053, or TB-012/T-059, T-060 mitigations. The patch says the dev-branch release lane moves from dispatch-only with a ref input to a push-to-dev trigger. It calls release-provider.yml with environment: dev and secrets: inherit. It says the signing job uses Developer ID and notarization with the five Apple signing secrets, and that other secrets are DEV_*. This is documentation of workflow behavior; .github/workflows/release-dev-branch.yml, release-provider.yml and scripts/test-release-dev-branch.py are not supplied, so I cannot verify them. Open question for integration or a human reviewer: whether the real workflow gates the Apple signing secrets, so that an untrusted push to dev cannot run attacker-controlled code with them. That would bear on T-013/T-034 (provider artifact trust) and the A-011 binary registry, since dev signing and publication use DEV_RELEASE_KEY rather than A-005. No finding is raised because there is no evidence of the workflow change. This doc-only change does not itself introduce a regression.
